issues.failure_explanation: The term S_2 A_2 multiplies a q by q matrix by an m by m matrix, which is undefined when q<m. The theorem's first condition is therefore ill-defined and cannot be applied as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first condition by the correct dimensionally consistent condition involving U_1, A_0, A_1, A_2 and S_1, and verify it before applying the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The block shift-and-deflate theorem is not a valid statement, so its application in Section 3 to construct \tilde A(z) lacks a well-defined justification.
issues.title: Ill-defined condition in Theorem th3.2
issues.why_classification: The theorem is a supporting result whose statement is ill-defined; correcting it is a local but necessary repair, and the subsequent construction can be checked directly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the sequences $\{ A_1^{(k)}\}_k$ and $\{ A_2^{(k)}\}_k$ are bounded and $\rho(\Lambda_{G,1})=|\lambda_{m-\ell}|<1$

issues.failure_explanation: Convergence of A_0^{(k)}W_{G,1} to 0 does not imply that W_{G,1} lies in the null space of A_0^{(k)} for any finite k. Exact nullity is an integer; a scalar or diagonal CR sequence can have the inside component tending to 0 while remaining nonzero, so the nullity can be 0 although m-\ell>0. The correct consequence is that the corresponding singular values tend to 0, not that the exact nullity equals m-\ell.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exact nullity statement by a statement that the last m-\ell singular values tend to 0 (or that the numerical rank tends to m-\ell), and adjust the SVD argument accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The exact rank/nullity guarantee used to justify partitioning the SVD of A_0^{(k)} and A_2^{(k)} is false; only numerical rank/singular value decay is supported.
issues.title: False exact nullity limit in Proposition prop:A0KW
issues.why_classification: The false exact nullity claim is not needed in exact form; a short local weakening to numerical rank preserves the algorithmic use of the SVD threshold.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, from Proposition \ref{prop:A0KW}, we can readily conclude that

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:A0KW only gives convergence of A_0^{(k)}W_{G,1} and T_{R,1}A_2^{(k)} and a (false) nullity statement. It does not prove that the right singular vectors V_{0,2}^{(k)} of A_0^{(k)} corresponding to the smallest singular values span an approximate invariant subspace of G. That requires a separate perturbation/separation argument, which is not supplied. The assertion that the displayed limit follows 'readily' is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lemma proving that the small singular subspace of A_0^{(k)} (resp. A_2^{(k)}) converges to the invariant subspace of G (resp. R), assuming the required singular-value separation.
issues.overall_effect: The SVD-based extraction of W_{G,1} and T_{R,1} in Algorithm alg:isg lacks a rigorous justification.
issues.title: Unsupported invariant-subspace approximation from SVD
issues.why_classification: The missing convergence result is nontrivial but standard; supplying it is a contained new lemma and does not change the overall algorithm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State \textbf{Input:} the $\ell\times \ell$ matrix coefficients $B_0$, $B_1$, and $B_2$ of the QME \eqref{eq:qmeB}.
\State \textbf{Output:} the solution $\bar{G}_{11}$ of the QME \eqref{eq:qmeB} with eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$.
Similarly, $\bar{R}_{11}$ is the only solution to \eqref{eq:qmeRbar} with eigenvalues $1/\mu_1,\ldots,1/\mu_\ell$.

issues.failure_explanation: The generalized Schur decomposition must be ordered so that the leading ell-dimensional deflating subspace corresponds to the solvent with eigenvalues mu_1,...,mu_ell. The algorithm as written gives no ordering rule, no input mu_i, and no check that the leading block yields the correct solvent rather than the other unit-circle solvent (or a subspace with singular Z_11). Thus it cannot guarantee the stated output.

failure_location.quote:
Compute the generalized Schur decomposition 
$$
Q^* M Z=T, \quad Q^* N Z=S
$$
with $Q$ and $Z$ unitary and $T$ and $S$ upper triangular, and where all matrices are partitioned as block $2 \times 2$ matrices with $\ell \times \ell$ blocks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify how to order the QZ decomposition (e.g., using known mu_i or a selection criterion for the desired deflating subspace) and check the required invertibility conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The central QZ step of BS-CR is not well defined and may compute the wrong solution or fail, undermining Algorithm alg:gfull.
issues.title: QZ algorithm does not select the desired solvent
issues.why_classification: The algorithm's output guarantee cannot be met from its stated inputs without adding a new selection step or input; this is central to the claimed method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\If{$\bar{A}_{122}$ in \eqref{21} is nonsingular}
        \State Compute $\bar{G}_{21}$ and $\bar{R}_{12}$ 
        by applying \eqref{G_21bar} and \eqref{R_12bar}, respectively.
        \EndIf
        \State Compute $G$ and $R$, 
        by means of \eqref{G_final} and \eqref{R_final}, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: The formulas for B_i and for recovering \bar G_{21} and \bar R_{12} require \bar A_{122} to be nonsingular. The algorithm computes B_i before checking this condition, and if \bar A_{122} is singular it skips computing \bar G_{21} and \bar R_{12} but still uses them in the final reconstruction formulas. The paper's assumptions do not guarantee nonsingularity of \bar A_{122}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add nonsingularity of \bar A_{122} as an explicit assumption/input check before computing B_i, and either handle or exclude the singular case; if excluded, do not proceed to the final reconstruction.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:gfull is not well defined and its output guarantee fails whenever \bar A_{122} is singular.
issues.title: BS-CR uses \bar A_{122}^{-1} before checking nonsingularity
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained additional condition/check, but it narrows the algorithm's guaranteed scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $a(z)$ has $\ell$ distinct roots $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$ of modulus $1$, each with multiplicity 2

issues.failure_explanation: Case 3 lists 1 and -1 twice among the eight mu_i. Thus the test case has only six distinct unit-modulus values, contradicting the paper's assumption that the mu_i are distinct. The claim that this example tests the method under the stated hypotheses for ell=8 is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the repeated values by distinct unit-modulus numbers so that eight distinct mu_i are used.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical evidence for the ell=8 case does not correspond to the paper's assumptions.
issues.title: Example 3 Case 3 violates distinctness assumption
